\paragraph{Synthesis.}
VLA fine-tuning redistributes instruction attention rather than reshaping visual geometry: training effects concentrate at the readout ($R^2$ $+0.069$, attention $+46$pp) rather than images ($\Delta \leq 1.7\%$).
This explains Grant et al.'s~\cite{grant2026} visual dominance finding: DINOv2 has the highest geometric alignment ($\rho = 0.692$), yet VLA readout surpasses it in decodability ($R^2 = 0.678$ vs.\ $0.634$).
Seven analyses support L1 attention redistribution: \emph{interventional} (dose-response, $d = 0.48 \to 0.64$; counterfactual, $d = 0.63$--$0.97$), \emph{supporting} (attention gradient $0 \to 9 \to 24$ heads; $R^2$ ablation $+0.059$; trajectory $d = 0.65$), and \emph{constraining} (bootstrap CIs, $p = 0.0018$; $R^2$ $z = -3.11$, $0$\textsuperscript{th} percentile).
Extended analysis in Appendix~\ref{sec:mechanistic_interpretation}--\ref{sec:functional_stages}.

\paragraph{Limitations and scope.}
We study OpenVLA-7B on held-out LIBERO; attention patterns may differ across scales (Appendix~\ref{sec:ood_diagnostics}).
Both architectures are causal-decoder; flow-matching~\cite{black2024_pi0} and diffusion~\cite{ghosh2024_octo} VLAs use cross-attention, so findings may not generalize to non-autoregressive decoders.
Llama-2's 9/32 pretrained instruction heads may reflect text bias ($+15$-head delta isolates fine-tuning).
All analyses are open-loop, as in concurrent VLA representation studies~\cite{grant2026,haon2025}; however, representational analysis has independent design value---our entry-exit profile yields a concrete diagnostic (L1 attention entropy monitoring during fine-tuning), and the readout-vs-image dissociation directly informs token pruning strategies.
Closed-loop validation on downstream task success is an orthogonal contribution and a natural next step.

2	We decompose OpenVLA-7B across all 32 LLM layers using cross-instruction probes, attention analysis, and functional probes, with factorial trained/pretrained/untrained controls on LIBERO.
3	Three findings emerge.

\paragraph{Convergent reorganization from opposite starting points.}
The two architectures start from dramatically different untrained profiles: OpenVLA peaks at L0 ($R^2 = 0.629$) then collapses to ${\approx}0$ at mid-layers, while Phi-3-V peaks at L6 ($0.578$) with gradual decline.
Yet training drives both to similar mid-layer peaks (OpenVLA L9: $0.637$; TraceVLA L11: $0.634$; $\Delta = 0.003$; overlapping CIs; Table~\ref{tab:2x2_r2}).
Peak $R^2$ values are comparable before and after training ($91$--$99\%$ of trained), but peak locations shift deeper (L0${\to}$L9; L6${\to}$L11) and deep-layer variance drops substantially (OpenVLA std $0.277 \to 0.040$; Phi-3-V $0.068 \to 0.011$).
This convergence from maximally different starting points---one architecture building from near-random representations, the other from instruction-tuned features---is consistent with VLA training discovering a common functional organization constrained by the causal-decoder design, though observed in only two architectures.
L1 probe accuracy \emph{decreases} in TraceVLA ($98.1\% \to 83.6\%$) despite more dominant heads ($28 \to 32$), replicating the information-computation dissociation in OpenVLA: increased attention to instructions does not imply increased decodable information.

VLA fine-tuning redistributes instruction attention rather than reshaping visual geometry: training effects concentrate at the readout ($R^2$ $+0.069$, attention $+46$pp) rather than images ($\Delta \leq 1.7\%$), explaining Grant et al.'s~\cite{grant2026} visual dominance finding ($\rho = 0.692$ for DINOv2, yet readout $R^2 = 0.678$ vs.\ $0.634$).

899	Per-layer profiles suggest three stages: redistribution (L0--L1; probe $99.6\%$, 24/32 instruction-dominant heads), computation (L8--L13; $R^2$ peak $0.655$--$0.678$), and decay (L14--L31, ${\sim}56\%$ of parameters; declining $R^2$ and RSA suggest pruning potential).
900	Task-specific fine-tuning eliminates L31 re-engagement (18 $\to$ 0 heads; \S\ref{sec:learned_routing}), consistent with exit-layer attention serving multi-task flexibility ($N{=}2$).
901	TraceVLA~\cite{zheng2024tracevla} (Phi-3-V) confirms convergent entry-exit attention concentration from an opposite starting point (\S\ref{sec:learned_routing}).
902	The $2 {\times} 2$ trained-vs-untrained comparison reveals convergent reorganization: untrained OpenVLA collapses from L0 ($R^2 = 0.629$) to near-zero at mid-layers (L20: $0.086$, std $= 0.277$), while untrained Phi-3-V peaks at L6 ($0.578$) with gradual decline (std $= 0.068$)---qualitatively opposite untrained landscapes.
903	Yet training drives both to nearly identical mid-layer peaks ($0.637$ vs.\ $0.634$, $\Delta = 0.003$) with stabilized deep-layer variance (OpenVLA std $0.277 \to 0.040$; Phi-3-V $0.068 \to 0.011$).
904	This convergent outcome from divergent starting points suggests that mid-layer action specialization is a robust attractor of VLA training, not an architectural artifact.
905	Exit-layer $R^2$ differs ($0.488$ vs.\ $0.557$), possibly reflecting architectural differences in late-layer processing.
906	Remaining predictions: cross-attention VLAs ($\pi_0$~\cite{black2024_pi0}, Octo~\cite{ghosh2024_octo}) should lack L1 instruction-dominant heads; larger VLAs should yield flatter per-head contributions.
907	For deployments, L1 instruction probes can flag instruction-discriminative tasks and L1 attention entropy can monitor instruction under-attendance at runtime.
